result.topic_en: Euler converts the alternating series $s=1/\alpha-1/\beta+1/\gamma-\dots$ into a continued fraction: he first expresses the auxiliary Fraktur quantities in terms of $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\dots$ and then derives the partial denominators $b,c,d,e,\dots$ explicitly.
result.transcription:

$s=\frac{1}{\alpha}-\frac{1}{\beta}+\frac{1}{\gamma}-\frac{1}{\delta}+\text{etc.}$
cuius quidem numeratores omnes sint vnitates signo $+$ et $-$ alternatim affectae, denominatores vero progressionem quamcunque constituant, quod tamen non obstat, quo minus omnes plane series in hac forma contineantur, siquidem termini seriei $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ non solum numeri fracti, sed etiam negatiui euadere possunt.

§. 10. Quo igitur fractionem continuam isti seriei aequalem eruamus, primo faciamus $\mathfrak{A}\mathfrak{B}=\alpha$, $\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{C}=\beta$, $\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{D}=\gamma$, et ita porro, vnde ob $\mathfrak{A}=1$ sequentes nanciscemur valores:
$\mathfrak{B}=\alpha;\qquad \mathfrak{C}=\frac{\beta}{\alpha};$
$\mathfrak{D}=\frac{\alpha\gamma}{\beta};\qquad \mathfrak{E}=\frac{\beta\delta}{\alpha\gamma};$
$\mathfrak{F}=\frac{\alpha\gamma\varepsilon}{\beta\delta};\qquad \mathfrak{G}=\frac{\beta\delta\zeta}{\alpha\gamma\varepsilon};$
$\mathfrak{H}=\frac{\alpha\gamma\varepsilon\eta}{\beta\delta\zeta};\qquad \mathfrak{I}=\frac{\beta\delta\zeta\theta}{\alpha\gamma\varepsilon\eta};$
etc. etc.
Nunc igitur tantum superest, vt ex his valoribus litterarum germanicarum ipsos indices $b, c, d, e$ fractionis continuae eliciamus.

§. 11. Ex formulis autem, quibus supra literae germanicae per indices fractionis continuae sunt determinatae vicissim ex his litteris ipsos indices $b, c, d, e, f$ etc. definiamus, ac reperiemus
$b=\mathfrak{B},\ c=\frac{\mathfrak{C}-\mathfrak{A}}{\mathfrak{B}},\ d=\frac{\mathfrak{D}-\mathfrak{B}}{\mathfrak{C}},\ e=\frac{\mathfrak{E}-\mathfrak{C}}{\mathfrak{D}},\ f=\frac{\mathfrak{F}-\mathfrak{D}}{\mathfrak{E}}$, etc.
Hos igitur valores ordine euoluamus, dum loco litterarum $\mathfrak{B}, \mathfrak{C}, \mathfrak{D}$, etc. formulas ante inuentas substituemus.

§. 12. Primo autem erat $\mathfrak{B}=\alpha$, vnde fit $b=\alpha$; deinde est
$\mathfrak{C}-$

145
$\mathfrak{C}-\mathfrak{A}=\frac{\beta-\alpha}{\alpha}$, vnde fit $c=\frac{\beta-\alpha}{\alpha\alpha}$.
Porro erit
$\mathfrak{D}-\mathfrak{B}=\frac{\alpha(\gamma-\beta)}{\beta}$, vnde fit $d=\frac{\alpha\alpha(\gamma-\beta)}{\beta\beta}$.
Deinde habebimus
$\mathfrak{E}-\mathfrak{C}=\frac{\beta(\delta-\gamma)}{\alpha\gamma}$ hincque $e=\frac{\beta\beta(\delta-\gamma)}{\alpha\alpha\gamma\gamma}$.
Simili modo ob
$\mathfrak{F}-\mathfrak{D}=\frac{\alpha\gamma(\varepsilon-\delta)}{\beta\delta}$ [?] $f=\frac{\alpha\alpha\gamma\gamma(\varepsilon-\delta)}{\beta\beta\delta\delta}$ [?].
Eodem modo ob
$\mathfrak{G}-\mathfrak{E}=\frac{\beta\delta(\zeta-\varepsilon)}{\alpha\gamma\varepsilon}$ erit $g=\frac{\beta\beta\delta\delta(\zeta-\varepsilon)}{\alpha\alpha\gamma\gamma\varepsilon\varepsilon}$
etc.
Hac igitur ratione indices fractionis continuae, quam quaerimus, sequenti modo erunt expressi:
$b=\alpha\qquad c=\frac{\beta-\alpha}{\alpha\alpha}$
$d=\frac{\alpha\alpha(\gamma-\beta)}{\beta\beta}\qquad e=\frac{\beta\beta(\delta-\gamma)}{\alpha\alpha\gamma\gamma}$
$f=\frac{\alpha\alpha\gamma\gamma(\varepsilon-\delta)}{\beta\beta\delta\delta}\qquad g=\frac{\beta\beta\delta\delta(\zeta-\varepsilon)}{\alpha\alpha\gamma\gamma\varepsilon\varepsilon}$
$h=\frac{\alpha\alpha\gamma\gamma\varepsilon\varepsilon(\eta-\zeta)}{\beta\beta\delta\delta\zeta\zeta}\qquad i=\frac{\beta\beta\delta\delta\zeta\zeta(\theta-\eta)}{\alpha\alpha\gamma\gamma\varepsilon\varepsilon\eta\eta}$
etc. etc.

§. 13. Tantum igitur opus est vt isti valores loco indicum $b, c, d, e, f$ etc. in fractione continua
$s=\cfrac{1}{b+\cfrac{1}{c+\cfrac{1}{d+\text{etc.}}}}$

items.quote: quod tamen non obstat, quo minus omnes plane series in hac forma contineantur, siquidem termini seriei $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ non solum numeri fracti, sed etiam negatiui euadere possunt.
items.english: This does not prevent absolutely all series from being contained in this form, since the terms $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ of the series may be not only fractions but also negative numbers.

items.quote: Quo igitur fractionem continuam isti seriei aequalem eruamus
items.english: In order to find the continued fraction equal to this series.

items.quote: Nunc igitur tantum superest, vt ex his valoribus litterarum germanicarum ipsos indices $b, c, d, e$ fractionis continuae eliciamus.
items.english: Now it only remains to extract the indices $b, c, d, e$ of the continued fraction from these values of the German (Fraktur) letters.

items.quote: quoniam vero isti valores sunt fracti, quo facilius formam a fractionibus partialibus liberemus, primum ex valoribus inuentis denominatores collamus
items.english: But since these values are fractions, in order to free the form more easily from partial fractions, let us first remove the denominators from the values found.
